column6: A member identifier is 1\u2013128 ASCII characters: the first a letter/digit, then letters/digits/`_`/`.`/`-`. This is the input profile of this lesson. The request parsing of the service doors is chapter 1.1 N2.1 (query, the JSON of the body, the path byte for byte, HTTP, early refusal); deviations are below. The order of checks: the frame (framing, the body limit 1 MiB \u2014 413) \u2192 route and method (404, 405) \u2192 identity (403) \u2192 body and membership (400, 409): an extra body larger than the limit with a foreign method \u2014 413 earlier than 404/405 (reconciliation of python and go \u041c10/6\u201311, B3). `HEAD` is not a method of the service doors: `/v1/status`, `/v1/join`, `/v1/leave`, `/metrics` \u2014 405, `/v1/write` and `/v1/rights` \u2014 404 by their owners, chapters 1.1 and 1.2 (both implementations, agreed without a norm). The bodies of service POSTs are one JSON object; unknown fields are rejected; the read limit is 1 MiB, the actual count of bytes, extra JSON/framing/truncation \u2014 400, exceeding \u2014 413, the read time is limited by the implementation. 400/404/405 \u2014 `BadRequestFault`, 403 \u2014 `ForbiddenFault`, 413 \u2014 `BodyTooLargeFault` of chapter 1.1. For own status/join/leave/write/metrics 503 is `UnavailableFault` before sending, `AmbiguousFault` after sending a change; at the connection limit \u2014 `UnavailableFault` with `Retry-After: 1` (chapter 1.1 N4). After an unknown join/leave the operator reads status; there is no automatic proof of success from a timeout. The floor keeps the replay memory of chapter 1.1.
